data.description:
## Description

**What**: Post-Phase-F leakage detector that scans the session branch for non-merge commits (which the S4 hook should have prevented but may exist via bypass), reads each commit's DSO-Story trailer, and routes it: valid trailer → cherry-pick to story/<id>; orphan trailer (DSO-Task or DSO-Bug only) → cherry-pick to story/orphan-<sprint-session-id>; missing trailer → hard-fail with manual-attribution prompt; closed-story trailer → hard-fail with named recovery options (rebase-and-retag with `git rebase -i` + manual trailer edit, or `--force-route-to=<story-id>` override flag); cherry-pick conflict → `git cherry-pick --abort` + hard-fail with conflicting commit SHA and named conflicting paths.
**Why**: Defense in depth — even with S4's pre-commit hook, sub-agents may bypass it via unusual paths. Deterministic recovery preserves attestation cleanliness.

**Scope**:
- IN: Detector script that scans session branch for non-merge commits
- IN: Trailer parser shared with S2
- IN: 5-case routing matrix as specified above
- IN: --force-route-to override flag for closed-story trailer recovery
- OUT: Pre-commit hook itself — owned by S4

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, test case 1: direct-edit attempted in session worktree with marker present is rejected at S4 hook (asserted via S4 test) — leakage detector not invoked
  ← Satisfies: "SC3 deterministic leakage handling"
- When this story is complete, test case 2: injected non-merge commit on session branch with valid DSO-Story trailer is cherry-picked to story/<id> successfully
  ← Satisfies: "SC3"
- When this story is complete, test case 3: injected non-merge commit with no DSO trailer triggers hard-fail with manual-attribution prompt
  ← Satisfies: "SC3"
- When this story is complete, test case 4: injected commit with closed-story DSO-Story trailer triggers hard-fail with named recovery options listed in stderr
  ← Satisfies: "SC3"
- When this story is complete, test case 5: cherry-pick conflict on a target story branch triggers `git cherry-pick --abort` and hard-fail with the conflicting commit SHA and named conflicting paths
  ← Satisfies: "SC3"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Cherry-pick conflicts on interleaved file edits have no automated resolution path. The hard-fail abort + named paths is the contract; do not introduce a silent-resolution code path.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sprint orchestrator, the leakage detector cherry-picks bypass commits to the correct story branch or hard-fails with named recovery options
